details: Bitwise Asset Management's Spot Hyperliquid ETF (BHYP) began trading on the New York Stock Exchange today, May 15, 2026. This ETF provides direct spot exposure to HYPE, the native token of Hyperliquid, a high-performance Layer 1 blockchain known for its on-chain trading and decentralized finance. The fund incorporates Bitwise's in-house staking infrastructure and features a 0.34% sponsor fee, waived for the first month on the initial $500 million in assets.
title: Bitwise Launches Spot Hyperliquid ETF (BHYP) on NYSE

details: The U.S. Senate Banking Committee voted 15-9 on May 14, 2026, to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act). This bipartisan approval, with two Democrats joining Republicans, represents a significant step towards establishing a federal regulatory framework for digital assets, aiming to clarify jurisdiction between the SEC and CFTC. The legislation seeks to protect consumers and encourage domestic innovation in the crypto space.
title: US Senate Committee Advances Key Crypto Regulatory Bill (CLARITY Act)

details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced substantial net outflows of $630.4 million on May 13, 2026. This marked the steepest single-day withdrawal since mid-February, with analysts suggesting that corporate treasury buyers have reduced their activity. This trend indicates that some institutional participants may be treating recent price rallies as opportunities for liquidation rather than accumulation.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Significant Outflows Amid 'Rally Without Conviction'

details: Gemini Space Station, Inc. reported stable transaction revenue of $24.1 million for the first quarter of 2026. While exchange revenue saw a decrease, the company's services revenue and interest income increased by 122% year-over-year. Additionally, Winklevoss Capital Fund made a $100 million strategic investment in Gemini, which is expected to bolster its balance sheet and support ongoing product development and strategic initiatives.
title: Gemini Posts Stable Q1 Revenue, Secures $100M Strategic Investment

details: Ledger, a prominent crypto hardware wallet manufacturer, has reportedly postponed its plans for a U.S. Initial Public Offering (IPO), now considering private funding rounds as an alternative. Similarly, blockchain software company Consensys has also delayed its anticipated public listing. This indicates a broader trend within the digital asset sector where firms are re-evaluating public market entries due to lower token prices and subdued trading volumes.
title: Ledger, Consensys Postpone IPO Plans Due to Weak Crypto Market

details: The T3 Financial Crime Unit, a collaborative effort involving stablecoin issuer Tether, blockchain network Tron, and analytics firm TRM Labs, announced it has frozen over $450 million in illicit digital assets since its inception in September 2024. The unit reported a significant increase in intercepted illicit proceeds in 2025, targeting various crimes including terrorist financing, drug trafficking, and violent offenses.
title: Tether, Tron & TRM Financial Crime Unit Freezes $450M in Illicit Crypto Funds
